front: What is the right pedal of a piano called, and what does it do?
back: The damper (sustain) pedal. It lifts all the dampers so notes keep ringing.

front: Where is your foot when you pedal?
back: The ball of the foot is on the pedal and the heel stays on the floor.

front: When do you press the damper pedal relative to a chord?
back: Just after the chord is played, so only the new notes are caught.

front: What do Ped. and the asterisk mean in pedal marks?
back: Ped. means press the damper pedal. The asterisk means lift it.

front: What is legato pedalling?
back: Changing the pedal just after the new chord is played, so the sound stays connected and clean.

front: What does blur mean when pedalling?
back: Old and new notes sounding together because the pedal was held through a chord change.

front: Why change the pedal after the new chord and not at the same moment?
back: So the new notes are caught and the old chord is cut off.

front: What does the sostenuto (middle) pedal hold?
back: Only the notes whose keys are already down when the pedal is pressed.

front: What does una corda mean, and what cancels it?
back: Una corda means one string and tells you to use the left (soft) pedal. Tre corde cancels it.

front: What is half pedalling?
back: Pressing the damper pedal only partway so the dampers touch the strings lightly.

front: What is an Alberti bass?
back: A left-hand pattern that plays a chord as lowest, highest, middle, highest. On C: C, G, E, G.

front: What is a waltz bass?
back: A left-hand pattern in 3/4 with a low note on beat 1 and a chord on beats 2 and 3.

What is an open fifth?
back: A root and the note a fifth above it, with no third.

front: What is an add9 chord?
back: A triad with the 9th added. Cadd9 is C, D, E, G.

front: Name three features of the ambient piano style.
back: Slow tempo, wide spacing, and the pedal held across bars. Also open fifths, add9 colours and rests.

front: What is a sus2 chord?
back: A chord with the third replaced by the 2nd. Dsus2 is D, E, A.

front: What is a sus4 chord?
back: A chord with the third replaced by the 4th. Asus4 is A, D, E.

front: What are the frets of Cadd9 (strings 6 to 1)?
What are the frets of Asus2 (strings 6 to 1)?
What are the notes of Em7?
back: E, G, B, D.

front: What is a power chord?
back: A chord made of the root and the fifth, often with the root repeated an octave higher. It has no third.

front: Where is the G5 power chord with its root on string 6?
back: Frets 3 5 5 on strings 6, 5 and 4.

front: What is the shape of a movable power chord?
back: Root on string 6, then two frets higher on string 5 and two frets higher on string 4.

front: What is the bass note of a chord?
back: Its lowest note.

front: In C major, which chords are I and V?
back: I is C and V is G.

front: When does a progression come home?
back: When it ends on the I chord and settles there.

front: What is voicing?
back: Making one line of the music, usually the melody, louder than the others.

front: How do you bring out the top note of a right-hand chord?
back: Rest the arm weight on finger 5 and press the other keys lightly.

front: What is the key of Tchaikovsky's Old French Song, and how many flats?
back: G minor, with two flats (Bb and Eb).

front: What does the left hand do in bars 17 to 19 of Old French Song?
back: It plays short staccato broken chords while the right hand plays legato.

front: What is Travis picking?
back: A fingerstyle pattern in which the thumb alternates between two bass strings on every beat while the fingers play higher strings.

front: Which strings does the thumb play on a C chord in Travis picking?
back: Strings 5 and 4, alternating.

front: In the count 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &, which counts does the thumb play?
back: The numbers, 1 2 3 4. The fingers play the ands.

front: What is a ringing arpeggio?
back: An arpeggio where each note is allowed to sound until the chord changes.

front: What does a capo on fret 2 do to the Asus2 shape?
back: It sounds as Bsus2 (B, C#, F#), a whole step higher.
